objective: Implement the bounded M1 gameplay-systems slice without changing stage choreography, PatternDefinition/BossPhaseDefinition public interfaces, menus, saves, replay formats, art, audio, or the frozen v3 plan. First, make the six selectable shot types behaviorally distinct using the existing controls: Miko A is wide tracking while unfocused, but focus narrows its acquisition cone/range and improves effective accuracy; Miko B keeps yin-yang satellites separated at the sides while unfocused and pulls them inward into concentrated straight fire while focused; Magician A is wide stardust with a real close-range damage benefit and narrows while focused; Magician B is a true sustained piercing laser whose focused form is narrower and higher damage while unfocused is broader and lower damage; Swordswoman A is a close/mid-range fan with actual distance falloff and a narrow focused cross-slash; Swordswoman B launches blades outward and then returns them through enemies for a second hit, with the return path responding to lateral player movement. Extend player-bullet state and collision only as narrowly as needed; repeated-hit behavior must be deterministic and bounded. Provide a fixed-boss behavioral benchmark proving the six loadouts' standard kill times are within plus/minus 15 percent of the six-loadout mean while their coverage, positioning, and risk/reward behavior differ. Second, replace enemy item-type selection and initial item drift randomness with an authored deterministic drop contract: _spawn_enemy accepts/stores explicit drop item IDs from wave data, enemy defeat emits exactly that list in stable order, and a documented fixed compatibility list may be used only for legacy call sites until the later content-runtime ticket supplies every wave. The same enemy/drop specification must yield identical item types and initial trajectories regardless of gameplay RNG seed; do not use weighted drop rolls for runtime enemy defeats. Third, implement the M1 score/capture ledger: each active Night Festival Seal raises the multiplier by exactly 0.1 from 1.0 to a hard maximum of 2.0; actual player death resets the active multiplier to 1.0; Bomb never resets it; graze grants score only and never life or bomb fragments; resource fragments come only from authored item drops; a spell starts a capture attempt, any actual miss or Bomb invalidates it, timeout is not a capture, and clearing with no miss/no Bomb awards a deterministic bonus derived from card base value, remaining time, and the active Night Festival multiplier. Track last capture result, run capture counts, and highest reached multiplier in deterministic GameManager/runtime state, but do not build M6 Continue UI, persistence, result screens, or practice menus. Preserve M0 replay/hash determinism and existing public compatibility where reasonable. Add compact behavioral tests that exercise real shot specs/update/collision semantics, score and capture transitions, deterministic drops, graze resource invariants, and the TTK envelope rather than merely searching source text.

context: M0 fixed-tick, RNG, BulletWorld, state hashing, and replay seams are already approved; preserve their public contracts and deterministic state capture.

An actual miss occurs only after the deathbomb window is not rescued; pressing Bomb marks the current spell attempt immediately but must not reset the Night Festival multiplier.
Do not add new input actions. Do not implement M6 Continue UI, records persistence, result screens, or practice/replay browsing in this ticket.
